turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mr. Iyer, come and sit. I will check your pressure before the doctor calls you, sleeve up please.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Arre, all this for a small itch? It will go by itself only.

[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Pressure is one twenty-eight over eighty-two, pulse eighty-eight, and temperature thirty-six point eight. Oxygen is ninety-eight percent, breathing sixteen a minute. I will call the doctor in.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good afternoon, I am Dr. Menon. Your sister sounded worried on the phone. What is the problem?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): There is no problem, doctor. Just a little itching on the arms and a bit on the chest. I am absolutely fine.
[SEG0006] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He is not fine. He scratched the whole of last night and the skin is red. I had to drag him.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): When did this itching start?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): At the reception they served prawns and coconut chutney, and I also put that new cream, so it is one of those only. What to do.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): We will come to prawns and cream. I asked when. Which day did the rash begin?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Sunday morning. The function was Saturday night, so two days. Very mild, I am telling you.
[SEG0011] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Mild, he says. The bedsheet was red from all the scratching.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever, any swelling of the lips, any trouble with breathing?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever, lips are normal, breathing is fine. I even sat in office the whole of yesterday.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Your sister said something about a tooth and an antibiotic.

[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Wisdom tooth was paining last week, so the chemist gave Mox, those red and yellow capsules. I took them by mouth, two or three only, pain went, so I stopped. No point eating tablets for fun.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mox is amoxicillin. Was the strength two-fifty or five hundred, do you remember?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): I never look at the strip, doctor. It is lying in the kitchen drawer at home.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Then I will not invent a strength. Tell me about the cream your sister mentioned.
[SEG0019] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Pink tube, for the dry skin. He has been putting it on both arms since three days. New one, he never used it before.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): What name is on that pink tube?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): I only call it the pink cream. Chemist said moisturiser, very gentle. Maybe Cetaphil, maybe some other one. I left it at home.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Name is unclear, alright. Any other tablets — Crocin, pressure tablets, sugar tablets?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Crocin if a headache comes, one tablet, not daily. No sugar tablets, no pressure medicine. I am thirty-eight, not some chronic patient.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you have any allergy to a medicine or a food?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No allergy to anything. Full stop.

[SEG0026] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That is not correct, doctor. Around eight or nine years, they gave him penicillin for a throat infection and the whole body became red and itchy, just like this. Amma stopped it and said never penicillin again.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Sister, that was summer heat rash, don't start stories. I have taken so many tablets since college. There is no penicillin allergy.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): So one of you says no allergy at all, and one remembers a childhood rash with penicillin. I will record both. I cannot decide it sitting here.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Record whatever you like. This thing is from the office AC or something, it will vanish.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me look, sleeves up, and open the top button please.

[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Both forearms show red, slightly raised patches, and the upper chest as well. There are scratch marks. I do not see blisters, the lips are not swollen, and the throat looks clear.
[SEG0032] person_1 (NURSE): I saw his back while seating him, doctor. Faint red rash there also, not weeping.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Faint, exactly. You are all making a big case out of a faint thing.

[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me think aloud. Three things arrived together — prawns at the function, this new pink cream, and the amoxicillin. Any one of them can give an itchy rash, and I have no firm diagnosis.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): So it may be a drug rash from the Mox, or contact from the cream, or a reaction to something you ate. I cannot strike any of those out today.
[SEG0036] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He has already left the capsules, hasn't he?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): I stopped day before yesterday. Tooth is quiet. Why to start it again.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Please do not restart Mox, and keep off penicillin-type antibiotics until we understand this better. I am not putting an allergy stamp on you. I am only being careful.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Careful, careful. The itch is a small thing and everyone is writing essays.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): For the itch I will prescribe cetirizine, ten milligrams, by mouth, one at night, for five days. It only damps the itch. It will not tell us which thing caused it.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Five days for this? If you insist, give it. I might leave it after two days if the itch is gone.
[SEG0042] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will remind him at night. Left to himself he skips tablets and then argues with me.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Stop the pink cream from today. No new lotion on those patches, plain water is enough.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): The tube was not cheap, but fine, I will stop it. Such a waste, honestly.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the rash comes back after the cream is stopped, we might arrange a patch test to see whether that cream is the trigger. Not today. Only if it returns.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Patch test and all. I have a report due Monday, my boss will not accept I went for a test.
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does hot water, or sweating, make the itch worse?
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): The AC vent is right above my desk in the chartered accountancy firm, that is why the skin dries, and the boss is after that Monday report.
[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am asking again. Hot water or sweat — does the itching increase?
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Hot water is fine, sweat is no issue. Only at night it itches a little more, nothing dramatic.
[SEG0051] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): At night he is properly restless, doctor. You should see him.
[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright, a bit more at night. After the prawns, any loose motion, vomiting, tummy pain?
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Stomach is perfectly fine. No loose motion, no vomiting. I ate the office canteen lunch also, no problem.
[SEG0054] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good. Let me put the plan in one breath. Cetirizine at night for five days, stop the pink cream, and no more Mox.

[SEG0055] person_3 (DOCTOR): if the rash is not better in one week, come back and we can talk about the patch test then. If the lips swell or the breathing gets hard, do not wait the week, come the same day.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): One week is a long drama, but if my sister drags me I will show my face. Otherwise I am done.
[SEG0057] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We will come if it is still there. I am staying with him this week, Amma insisted.
[SEG0058] person_1 (NURSE): I will send the cetirizine slip to the pharmacy. It can make you sleepy, so do not drive after the night dose.
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): Sleepy also, on top of everything. Thank you, doctor. I told you from the beginning it is nothing.
[SEG0060] person_3 (DOCTOR): Take the five days properly, Mr. Iyer. Even a small rash deserves that much. You can go now.

spec.situation: Itchy rash after 'something I ate or the new cream or the antibiotic'; patient unsure which; a family member says the same happened with penicillin in childhood, patient denies. No firm diagnosis; patch test or antihistamine.
features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.

omissions.text: Current/possible trigger food exposure to prawns (served at the function the night before onset) was stated and is part of the differential but is not separately recorded as a suspected trigger/exposure.
Amoxicillin/Mox course details were more specific: patient took only 'two or three' oral capsules and stopped day before yesterday; strength was unknown and explicitly not invented.

Pink cream timing/detail is slightly wrong: family said he had been applying the new pink tube to both arms for three days, but the recorded status says 'currently_used' even though the doctor told him to stop it from today.
Patient denied taking diabetes medicines and blood pressure medicines when specifically asked about other tablets.
Family-reported severity/detail of symptoms is missing: he scratched all night, skin was red, bedsheet was red from scratching, and at night he was 'properly restless'.
Rash distribution detail missing from symptom history: patient reported itching on the arms and 'a bit on the chest'; nurse also noted faint rash on the back.
Patient stated he sat in the office the whole of yesterday despite symptoms, indicating no functional limitation from breathing or systemic illness at that time.
Past suspected penicillin reaction timing detail is missing: family said this occurred around eight or nine years ago during treatment for a throat infection.
Doctor explicitly said he was not labeling a confirmed penicillin allergy yet: 'I am not putting an allergy stamp on you. I am only being careful.'

Examination detail missing: the doctor examined the throat and found it clear, and lips not swollen, as part of assessment for more serious reaction; throat finding is recorded, but that this was part of airway/angioedema concern is not captured.
Doctor advised plain water only on the rash patches after stopping the cream.
